title: The Russian Revolution
subject: histoire
description: In less than eight months, Russia passed from the power of the Tsars to that of the Bolsheviks. 1917 invents a model that will divide the world for decades.

hero.hook: In eight months, a thousand-year-old empire is toppled... and the 20th century is split in two.

blocks.text: In **1917**, in less than eight months, Russia went from an absolute monarchy to a regime led by the **bolsheviks**, a revolutionary party led by **Vladimir Lenin**. This is not a simple uprising. It is the collapse of an empire under the weight of war, then the fall into emptiness.
This shift invents a model that will divide the world for a large part of the 20th century.

Committed to the  since 1914, Russia is no longer following. Already **1.7 million** dead soldiers. Mutinies. Shortages of flour and coal in **Petrograd**, the capital (now St. Petersburg). Tsar **Nicholas II** refuses the reforms requested by the , the Russian parliament. [[World War I]] [[Douma]]

blocks.caption: Nicholas II, last tsar of a monarchy running out of steam.

blocks.text: The poison intended to kill , an influential monk at court, would have been neutralized by the sugar in the cakes where it had been slipped: the legend of his assassination says a lot about the discredit of the throne. [[Rasputin]]
By taking command at the front in **1915**, the tsar becomes solely responsible for the defeats. Rasputin's influence on Tsarina **Alexandra** ultimately ruined the prestige of the imperial family.

sections.title: February: the end of the Romanovs

blocks.text: In **February 1917** (according to the  then in use in Russia, delayed by several days in the West), the revolution started from bread. The workers take to the streets. The garrison fraternizes. Nicholas II abdicates on **March 2**: **Z** 300 years of reign of the Romanov dynasty come to an end. [[Julian calendar]]

blocks.caption: Petrograd 1917: the street takes precedence over the throne.

blocks.text: A “double power” then sets in. On the one hand, a legal **Provisional Government**. On the other, the , a council of workers and soldiers which controls factories and barracks. **Alexander Kerensky**, provisional figure, keeps Russia in the war. The people want peace, bread and land. [[The Petrograd Soviet]]

Lenin returns from exile in a “lead train” organized by Germany, which hopes to weaken Russia. From April, his s are banging: **“Peace, Bread, Earth”**. With , an outstanding organizer, the Bolsheviks prepared the insurrection. [[April Theses]] [[Leon Trotsky]]

blocks.caption: Lenin, strategist of an organized takeover.

blocks.text: When the Winter Palace was taken, the tsars' wine cellars were so vast that guards had to be posted to prevent the revolution from descending into drunkenness.

On the night of **November 7, 1917** (October 25 according to the Russian calendar), bridges, stations and telegraphs fell almost without a shot being fired. The Winter Palace, seat of the Provisional Government, follows. Then begins a bloody civil war until **1922**.

The **Cheka**, political police of the Bolsheviks, launches terror. In July **1918**, the imperial family was executed in Yekaterinburg. The Peace of  removes Russia from the war at the cost of heavy territorial losses. In **1922**, the **USSR** was born, the first state built on the , the ideology which combines the ideas of Marx and the method of Lenin. [[Brest-Litovsk]] [[Marxism-Leninism]]

blocks.text: In **1917**, the collapse of tsarism and the Bolshevik takeover transformed a bread revolt into the birth of the world's first communist state.
